claim: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an autosomal-recessive disorder induced by loss-of-function mutations in the gene encoding for cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) protein.
source: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an autosomal-recessive disorder induced by loss-of-function mutations in the gene encoding for cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) protein (Collins, 1992).
evidence: Supported by citation to Collins, 1992

claim: Defects in CFTR negatively influence homeostasis of airway surface liquid and mucus of the respiratory epithelium, aggravating mucociliary clearance.
source: Defects in CFTR negatively influence homeostasis of airway surface liquid and mucus of the respiratory epithelium, aggravating mucociliary clearance (Boucher, 2007; Gustafsson et al., 2012).

claim: CFTR modulators have achieved clinical improvements in people with at least one F508del mutation.
source: Despite the clinical improvements achieved by CFTR modulators in people with at least one F508del mutation (Middleton et al., 2019), chronic pulmonary infections with the opportunistic pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa (Pa) will continue to determine disease progression in untreated or unresponsive CF (Koch, 2002; Emerson et al., 2002).

claim: Chronic pulmonary infections with Pseudomonas aeruginosa will continue to determine disease progression in untreated or unresponsive CF.

claim: Long-term application of antibiotics promotes the emergence of persister populations.

claim: Long-term application of antibiotics promotes the emergence of multiple drug-resistant (MDR) bacteria.

claim: BPI is highly active against Gram-negative bacteria.

claim: BPI acts as an anti-inflammatory mediator by neutralizing Gram-negative lipopolysaccharide (LPS).

claim: BPI is one of the most effective antimicrobials in the human body.

claim: Preserved LPS neutralization and bactericidal activity was previously described for BPI orthologues derived from the Pacific oyster.

claim: Preserved LPS neutralization and bactericidal activity was previously described for BPI orthologues derived from ray finned fish (Actinopterygii).

claim: scoBPI comprised the highest number of cationic amino acids arginine, histidine, and lysine in regions I-III compared to nine other Actinopterygii BPI sequences.

claim: Only 15 amino acids in region II determine the antimicrobial activity in huBPI.

claim: scoBPI displayed a highly condensed positively charged cluster exclusively at the N-terminal tip.

claim: Levels of BPI in the sera were comparable among PwCF and an age- and sex-matched control group.

source: While levels of BPI in the sera were comparable among PwCF and an age- and sex-matched control group (Figure 2B), BPI-ANCA as measured in arbitrary units (AU) were significantly increased in PwCF (control: mean 314.8 AU, 95% confidence interval [CI] 209.3–420.4 AU; CF: mean 2218.0 AU, 95% CI 1271.0–3166.0 AU, p<0.0001; Figure 2C).

claim: Activity of scoBPI against Ec DH10B was in low picomolar range (IC50 0.032 ± 0.006 nM).

claim: Acipenser ruthenus (sterlet) BPI (acBPI) presented a cluster of positive charges at the N-terminal tip along with a relatively high quantity of basic amino acids in functional regions I–III.
source: Within the investigated class of Actinopterygii, acBPI of the sterlet Acipenser ruthenus (subclass Chondrostei) and gaBPI of the Atlantic cod Gadus morhua (subclass Neopterygii) also presented a cluster of positive charges in the respective area along with a relatively high quantity of basic amino acids in functional regions I–III (Figure 1—figure supplements 1B and 2A).
evidence: Supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 1B and 2A

source: Within the investigated class of Actinopterygii, acBPI of the sterlet Acipenser ruthenus (subclass Chondrostei) and gaBPI of the Atlantic cod Gadus morhua (subclass Neopterygii) also presented a cluster of positive charges in the respective area along with a relatively high quantity of basic amino acids in functional regions I–III (Figure 1—figure supplements 1B and 2A).
evidence: Supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplements 1B and 2A

claim: Overall sequence identity of acBPI with scoBPI was comparably low at 56.4%.
source: Interestingly, overall sequence identity with scoBPI was comparably low (56.4 and 62.8%, respectively; Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B

claim: Overall sequence identity of gaBPI with scoBPI was comparably low at 62.8%.
source: Interestingly, overall sequence identity with scoBPI was comparably low (56.4 and 62.8%, respectively; Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).

claim: scoBPI is a distantly related, orthologous protein to huBPI that combines LPS-neutralizing capacity and bactericidal activity towards MDR Pa isolates.
source: Collectively, we define scoBPI as a distantly related, orthologous protein to huBPI that combines LPS-neutralizing capacity and bactericidal activity towards MDR Pa isolates.
evidence: Supported by experimental data on LPS neutralization and bacterial killing

claim: scoBPI holds strong anti-inflammatory properties towards Ec and Pa LPS.
source: These data suggest that scoBPI holds strong anti-inflammatory properties towards Ec and Pa LPS.
evidence: Supported by experimental data on cytokine inhibition

claim: The affinity of BPI orthologues towards LPS is roughly determined by the respective quantity of basic amino acids.
source: Therefore, we hypothesized that the affinity towards LPS is roughly determined by the respective quantity of basic amino acids.
evidence: Based on inference from the known role of cationic regions in LPS binding

claim: scoBPI has a higher quantity of positively charged surface areas compared to mammalian muBPI or the distantly related osBPI.
source: In conclusion, this initial screen revealed a higher quantity of positively charged surface areas for scoBPI and other fish BPI compared to the mammalian muBPI or the distantly related osBPI.
evidence: Supported by structural analysis and electrostatic surface potential calculations

claim: Orthologous proteins muBPI and scoBPI do not contain epitopes detected by intrinsic BPI-ANCA of the tested cohort of PwCF.
source: Thus, the orthologous proteins muBPI and scoBPI do not contain epitopes detected by intrinsic BPI-ANCA of the tested cohort of PwCF.
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing no recognition by BPI-ANCA

claim: The benefits of administration of scoBPI by joining antimicrobial activity and LPS neutralization could potentially extenuate inflammation and tissue destruction.
source: Therefore, the benefits of administration of scoBPI by joining antimicrobial activity and LPS neutralization, including reduction of TNF release, could potentially extenuate inflammation and, thereby, tissue destruction.
evidence: Based on inference from the dual mechanism of action

claim: One limitation of clinical use of scoBPI might be a possible induction of antibodies against scoBPI during long-term or repeated applications.
source: Concerning clinical use, one limitation might be a possible induction of antibodies against scoBPI during long-term or repeated applications.
evidence: Based on speculation about potential immune responses

claim: Therapeutic use of scoBPI may rather be indicated in short-term settings.
source: Therefore, therapeutic use may rather be indicated in short-term settings.
evidence: Based on inference from potential immunogenicity concerns

claim: Actinopterygii BPI other than scoBPI may also bear therapeutic potentials.
source: Therefore, Actinopterygii BPI other than scoBPI may also bear therapeutic potentials and should be tested functionally.
evidence: Based on inference from structural similarities observed in other fish BPI
